claims: Changing a memory representation must not change the stable source address.
The deterministic baseline must remain available when a semantic profile is added.
Semantic and exact recovery are distinct success conditions.
Only R4 may declare exact recovery when the original source is present.
AI analyzers and decoders must disclose their identities and contracts.
Token overlap is a transparent baseline metric rather than canonical semantic truth.
Coordinate fidelity must be measured separately from text overlap.
Representation size and recovery quality should be evaluated together.
intent: define and experimentally compare deterministic and AI-assisted multi-resolution memory profiles
summary: ISQL-MEM v0.2 separates immutable byte-derived address identity from replaceable deterministic or AI-assisted memory representations and measures recovery quality by resolution.
uncertainty: exact-label coordinate metrics do not capture paraphrase equivalence
learned semantic distance remains a future derived metric
